newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to go on holiday in July - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to go on holiday in July - spokesman.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will go on a planned holiday in the second week of July, his press secretary said on Wednesday, adding that the Kremlin leader would spend it in Russia but was still unsure where.
"As for a holiday, it is planned, that's normal," Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference, adding that Yeltsin would not go to his once favourite destination, the Black Sea resort of Sochi.
In April the 66-year-old leader cut short a holiday in Sochi and the Kremlin blamed bad weather though television pictures from the area showed sunshine at the time.

In previous years Yeltsin spent much of his time in Sochi swimming and playing tennis, something which he seems as yet unwilling to do after a quintuple heart bypass operation last November and a bout of double pneumonia in January.
Yastrzhembsky offered no comment on Yeltsin's state of health other than to say that the holiday was a normal, planned event which would follow a number of important working meetings.

Yeltsin returned to active work in February and has generally maintained a busy schedule, though every now and then he escapes to his country residences outside Moscow for a day or two where he does paperwork, the Kremlin says.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin would attend the signing ceremony of a peace agreement for the Tajik civil war on Friday and would receive visiting Azeri President Haydar Aliyev before going on holiday.
Yeltsin returned to Moscow on Monday after attending a summit of the Group of Seven main industrialised nations in the U.S. city of Denver.

Yeltsin hailed the summit as a success for Russia, which won admission to the Paris Club of creditor nations and gained the backing of G7 leaders for its bid to join other global economic organisations.

But he also sparked off fresh concern about his health on Saturday when he missed a late-night gala concert. He resurfaced on Sunday looking well and refreshed and aides said he had just been tired after a heavy schedule of talks.
